title: Adam Savage's Tested
description:
Adam Savage’s Tested is a content platform and community playground for makers and curious minds. On Tested.com, the highly- engaged Tested YouTube channel, and at conventions and events, dynamic makers share ideas and inspire each other to build their obsessions. Led by Adam Savage, the Tested team explores the intersection of science, popular culture, and emerging technology, showing how we are all makers. Adam also takes viewers behind the scenes of films, TV shows, theater, and museums, shining a spotlight on the craftspeople and artists who make the magic we all enjoy.

Tested is also: Norman Chan, Joey Fameli, Josh Self, Kristen Lomasney and Thomas Crenshaw.

episodes.title: Adam Savage Explores the World's Largest Library
episodes.description:
Adam Savage goes inside the stunning Thomas Jefferson Building at the Library of Congress!  Guided by LOC chief of staff Ryan Ramsey, Adam tours the world’s largest library — home to more 184 million items, including the Gutenberg Bible, Lincoln's copy of the Gettysburg Address, Thomas Jefferson's personal book collection, soaring Beaux-Arts architecture and a physical card catalog holding 22 million cards. Join Adam as he explores the United States'  "palace to knowledge" for the first time, just steps from the U.S. Capitol. Have you ever visited the Library of Congress?

episodes.title: This Hardware Built Star Wars!
episodes.description:
When Industrial Light & Magic closed its Kerner Boulevard facility, Adam Savage stepped in to preserve a piece of cinematic history: the original parts and materials racks. Joined by legendary model maker Lorne Peterson, Adam takes a deep dive into the physical organization, problem-solving methodologies and materials — from Plastruct shapes and domes to model kit greeblies — that built the original Star Wars trilogy and other iconic films. Lorne shares incredible behind-the-scenes stories, including fabricating phone booths out of plastic domes to escape shop noise, the transition from LA to San Rafael, and the creative camaraderie that defined the golden age of practical visual effects. What do you think of ILM's parts organization?

episodes.title: The Reason This Space Docking Module Was Androgynous
episodes.description:
Adam Savage visits Smithsonian’s @airandspace Mary Baker Engen Restoration Hangar to examine a piece of Cold War space history: the APAS-75 (Androgynous Peripheral Assembly System) from the 1975 Apollo-Soyuz Test Project (ASTP). As Apollo curator Dr. Teasel Muir-Harmony and conservator Elizabeth Beesley explain, this module -- designed during the Cold War -- served as a universal airlock and docking interface that not only bridged two different spacecraft, but two radically different engineering philosophies as well. From contrasting U.S. and Soviet machining styles to bilingual Russian/English cockpit labeling to the conservation challenges of deteriorating insulation, join Adam for an inside look at the hardware that made history's most famous handshake in space possible. What do you think of the "androgynous" solution?
